summary.headline: Q4 FY26 order intake of INR86.1bn (+188% YoY) lifted backlog to INR214.6bn; Q4 EBITDA margin hit a record 27.2%.
summary.overview: GE Vernova T&D India reported a strong Q4 and full FY26, with revenue up 42% YoY in Q4 to INR16.4bn and 45% for the year to INR62.1bn. Profit before tax and exceptional items for FY26 rose to INR17.1bn from INR8.2bn, and the company ended the year with zero debt and about INR25bn of cash. Order intake was lifted by a large HVDC turnkey order from Adani Energy (VSC technology), and management guided to a mid-20s EBITDA margin for FY27. Management also announced a INR550mn disconnector and drives capacity at Vallam, Tamil Nadu, and a INR10 per share dividend.

segments.name: Domestic vs export
segments.commentary: Export orders in FY26 were about INR12bn versus INR32bn in FY25, which included one large export order; excluding large orders, base export orders grew 15-20%. Export was about 30% of FY25 revenue and new orders were about 92% domestic.

segments.name: Customer mix
segments.commentary: Backlog is 98% private customers, central utilities and PSUs; state utility exposure is under 2%.

segments.name: HVDC and projects
segments.commentary: A large HVDC turnkey order (Adani Energy, VSC) was booked in Q4, with execution mainly from FY28-29 onwards. Management does not disclose project versus product split.

guidance_outlook: Management endeavours to deliver mid-20s EBITDA margin going forward, after earlier guiding to low-20s and then mid-20s/high-20s in FY26.
Base order inflow expected to be around INR70bn (INR7,000 crore) and management remains confident of achieving it.
Two pending export RPT orders: a large export order where the decision is expected in H2 FY27, and a U.S. data-centre high-voltage order (about INR14-15bn) expected to be decided in Q1 FY27.
U.K. Grid Solutions purchase order (intra-group, feeding the Adani HVDC project) expected to be placed in the current quarter; it will not appear in the company's order book.
Capex of more than INR10bn to be phased from early FY27 through FY28, self-funded.
Management declined to give a split of Adani HVDC execution in early years; it said first two years would be lower than 30% and mostly engineering and supply-chain work.
capex_capacity: More than INR10bn of capex initiated across multiple product lines and facilities, to be phased through 2028.

INR550mn approved by the Board for new disconnector and drives capacity at Vallam, Tamil Nadu; disconnectors are being restarted for the Indian market, and some products will be global feeder factory output.
Air core reactor facility and HVDC thyristor valves and controls facility planned in India to raise local content.
Management did not give a revenue ballpark for the expanded capacity, citing that HVDC revenue depends on bought-out equipment and manpower rather than in-house capacity.
demand_pricing: Management says the TBCB pipeline has about 33 packages bid out, 21 of them at 765 kV; the only live HVDC tender is Barmer, whose bid deadline is being extended.
Data centres in India are about 1.5 GW installed, mostly at 220 kV; management expects a meaningful contribution once 400 kV and 765 kV data centres scale.
Transformer contracts carry price escalation clauses; for other products, cost inflation is built into tender pricing.
Management said Q4 domestic order finalisation was slightly dull, which it described as a conscious decision.

qa_highlights.question: Are export orders weak after FY25, and how will the RPT approvals translate into orders in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said excluding one large FY25 order, base export orders grew 15-20%. The pending RPT orders are a large export order (decision in H2 FY27), a U.S. data-centre order of about INR14-15bn (decision expected in Q1 FY27), and a U.K. Grid Solutions purchase order (intra-group).

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin outlook for FY27 and what was the INR50mn Q4 other expense item?
qa_highlights.answer: Management maintains an endeavour toward mid-20s EBITDA margin. The Q4 other expenses included about INR500mn of notional mark-to-market loss on foreign currency derivatives; management agreed EBITDA would have been better without it.

qa_highlights.question: Is Prolec's U.S. low-voltage distribution strategy relevant to the Indian entity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said India has no distribution-transformer manufacturing set-up, and entering would need organic or inorganic capacity; it said it does not see that as a current strategy.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Adani HVDC execution profile and the Barmer/South Kalamb project share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said early-year execution would be lower than 30%, with most revenue from FY29. For Barmer-type projects, the supplier share depends on line length and scope, not a fixed rule of thumb.

qa_highlights.question: Will HVDC refurbishment projects move from LCC to VSC?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said LCC-to-LCC refurbishment only requires valves and controls changes, whereas LCC-to-VSC is a wider scope with higher shutdown requirement and capex; it depends on customer choice.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company likely to sustain high margins and growth for longer?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the cycle is broader this time, covering the U.S., Europe, Middle East and Australia, and that export exposure is meaningful; it did not give a timeline for margin moderation.

risks_watch: Customer decision delays on large export RPT orders (H2 FY27 for one, Q1 FY27 for the U.S. order) and their conversion to revenue.
HVDC pipeline timing: Barmer bid deadline keeps being extended, and the next project after Barmer is not clearly scheduled.
Execution of the Adani HVDC turnkey order depends on securing a supply chain, with revenue weighted to FY29 onwards.
Imports of HVDC components (thyristor valves, controls hardware) remain, so local content is still limited until the new facility comes up.
Foreign-exchange derivative mark-to-market charges can affect other expenses and quarterly EBITDA.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, backlog and margins, but cautious on timing: management repeatedly declined to give quantified guidance on HVDC phasing, pipeline timing and export mix, and said quarterly order intake can be lumpy.
key_quotes: So, yes, we remain confident on achieving the base order number of INR7,000 crores.
Our order book remained strong in Q4, and we saw a booking of INR86.1 billion, up by 188% year-on-year compared to INR29.9 billion in quarter ended March '25.
During the fourth quarter, we achieved a record EBITDA margin of 27.2%.
So, this time, the cycle is different. The market is different and the longevity of the cycle looks to be more sustainable.

growth.why: Management guides mid-20s EBITDA margin for FY27 (held) and base order intake of about INR70bn (INR7,000 crore, held), backed by a INR214.6bn backlog and Q4 orders up 188%, with INR550mn Vallam capacity approved and a more-than-INR10bn capex programme phased through 2028 that is partly unquantified, so backing is partial.
